status_semantics.verified-local: Full stated Lean declaration is proved in this repository.
status_semantics.verified-imported: Full stated declaration is a compiled consumer of a pinned upstream certificate.
status_semantics.verified-core: A precisely delimited downstream core is proved; named analytic or representation bridges remain.
status_semantics.future-target: Exact target is identified but no trusted declaration is claimed.
status_semantics.cited-only: The manuscript delegates the result; source selection or a research-scale proof remains.

targets.book_ref: Appendix A, symmetric and asymmetric parts
targets.scope: The symmetric part of a preorder is an equivalence relation; its strict part is asymmetric and transitive.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Reflexivity and transitivity for the symmetric part; transitivity alone for strict-part transitivity.

targets.scope: Every nonempty finite set has a greatest element under a complete transitive relation.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite nonempty carrier subset, completeness, transitivity.

targets.scope: Transitive closure is transitive and is the least transitive extension.
targets.weakest_assumptions: An arbitrary binary relation.

targets.scope: Every partial order has a linear extension.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Reflexive, transitive, antisymmetric relation; classical choice enters through Mathlib's Zorn proof.

targets.scope: The compensated price-demand inner product is nonpositive in the exact sign-represented preference model.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Positive original prices, at least one good, asymmetric and strictly increasing preference function, and demand at the original and compensated budgets. Positivity of the new price is not consumed by the inequality proof.
targets.missing_bridge: The manuscript's strict inequality for unequal single-valued WARP demand requires a separate exact bridge from its WARP convention.

targets.scope: Maximization of one transitive relation rules out a strict direct revealed-preference reversal.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Choice is exactly the set of greatest elements; transitivity. Completeness is not consumed by the proof.

targets.scope: Utility demand is homogeneous of degree zero in prices and wealth.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Positive common scale; no continuity, convexity, or uniqueness.

targets.scope: A demanded bundle exhausts its budget.
targets.weakest_assumptions: At least one good, positive prices, strict coordinatewise monotonicity, utility maximization.

targets.scope: UMP existence, compact-valued upper-hemicontinuous demand, and continuous indirect utility.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Continuous utility, positive prices and wealth, Euclidean nonnegative orthant.
targets.missing_bridge: Package a compact budget correspondence and its lower-hemicontinuity proof, then apply Berge.

targets.scope: On an explicit admissible price domain, an attained expenditure value is homogeneous along admissible positive rays and concave along admissible mixtures; each Hicksian minimizer is a supergradient relative to that domain.
targets.weakest_assumptions: A nonempty admissible price set P; exact attained minimization over a price-independent upper-contour set only for prices in P; membership of the scaled price or convex combination only for the corresponding conclusion.
targets.missing_bridge: Existence/continuity of the expenditure value and differentiable Shephard/Roy/Slutsky corollaries remain analytic targets.

targets.scope: Finite GARP, positive Afriat inequalities, and regular utility rationalization are equivalent; the lower-envelope utility is constructive.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Pinned WGARP Dataset: finite nonempty observations, at least two goods, positive prices, nonzero nonnegative choices.
targets.missing_bridge: Document the encoding from the manuscript's dataset convention to WGARP.Dataset when the full Appendix B statement is frozen.

targets.book_ref: Chapter 3 and Appendix B, WGARP and coherent CMU
targets.scope: The pinned finite-data Theorem 1 proves the five adjacent equivalences among asymmetric continuous preference-function rationalization, a finite coherent-CMU normal form, a skew-symmetric matrix/simplex CMU normal form, WGARP, pairwise Afriat feasibility, and pairwise Varian feasibility.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite nonempty observations; at least two goods; strictly positive prices; nonzero nonnegative observed bundles; the exact finite and matrix/simplex CMU structures defined by the pinned WGARP project.
targets.missing_bridge: Relate the imported finite and matrix/simplex CMU normal forms to the manuscript's broader hyperspace formulation of arbitrary compact coalition structures; the local theorem deliberately does not claim this type-level equivalence.

targets.book_ref: Chapter 3 and Appendix B, WARP and strict coherent CMU
targets.scope: WARP is characterized by asymmetric strictly star-concave preference functions and the corresponding strict coherent-CMU representations.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite nonempty observations; at least two goods; strictly positive prices; nonzero nonnegative observed bundles; the cited theorem's exact strict star-concavity and strict-concavity conventions.
targets.missing_bridge: The pinned WGARP package contains no WARP or strict-star-concavity theorem; freeze those definitions and formalize the separate strict representation argument before claiming Lean coverage.

targets.scope: Independence and mixture continuity characterize finite expected utility with positive-affine uniqueness.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite nonempty prize space, all lotteries, complete/transitive preference, independence, mixture continuity.
targets.missing_bridge: Build a simplex API and the affine representation theorem; a statement skeleton is not counted.

targets.scope: A finite monotone coupling implies the expected-utility inequality for every increasing Bernoulli utility.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite preordered prize space, nonnegative coupling with the stated marginals and monotone support.
targets.missing_bridge: Prove the finite one-dimensional equivalence between CDF dominance and existence of a monotone coupling; general measures remain separate.

targets.scope: Feasibility test for risk-averse expected-utility rationalization.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Must be frozen from the cited Polisson-Quah-Renou theorem.
targets.missing_bridge: Exact source theorem and boundary/interior KKT convention.

targets.scope: Common wealth slope aggregates Marshallian demand through prices and total wealth.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Differentiable Gorman-form indirect utilities with a common positive wealth slope and Roy conditions.
targets.missing_bridge: Formalize Roy's identity or state the demand-level affine special case.

targets.scope: The ratio of two retained multinomial-logit probabilities is the exponential utility-index difference.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite nonempty alternative set and a strictly positive common logit scale μ.

targets.scope: Gradient of expected maximum utility equals choice probabilities under no ties.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite alternatives, integrable shocks, almost-sure unique maximizer; differentiability at the target index.
targets.missing_bridge: Measure-theoretic interchange/envelope infrastructure.

targets.scope: On an explicit admissible price domain, an attained profit value is homogeneous along admissible positive rays and convex along admissible mixtures; maximizers are relative subgradients and are efficient at positive prices.
targets.weakest_assumptions: A nonempty admissible price set P; exact attained maximization over a price-independent production set only for prices in P; scaled-price or mixture membership only where used; positive prices only for efficiency.
targets.missing_bridge: Topological conditions guaranteeing finite attained profit and differentiable Hotelling supply.

targets.scope: Existence, uniqueness, and planner equivalence in the maintained quasilinear market.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Exact endpoint, curvature, and tail conditions from the chapter's assumption box.
targets.missing_bridge: Intermediate-value and strict-monotonicity assembly after the assumptions are frozen.

targets.scope: A common supporting price and market clearing rule out a Pareto-improving market-clearing allocation.
targets.weakest_assumptions: A finite consumer type, market clearing, and weak and strict price-support inequalities. A global Nonempty consumer instance is not needed because a claimed Pareto improvement already supplies a strict improver.
targets.missing_bridge: Derive the price-support inequalities from utility maximization, budget exhaustion, transitivity, and local nonsatiation in the manuscript's exact model.

targets.scope: A Pareto optimum can be supported by prices and transfers.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Convex preferences/technology plus the exact closedness, properness, and cheaper-bundle assumptions selected for Appendix B.
targets.missing_bridge: Separation theorem and positive-price upgrade.

targets.scope: Existence in finite pure exchange.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Precise Arrow-Debreu fixed-point formulation must be selected.
targets.missing_bridge: Correspondence fixed point, boundary demand, and market-clearing proof.

targets.scope: Nonsingular normalized excess-demand Jacobian implies local uniqueness.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Differentiability near the equilibrium and nonsingular reduced Jacobian.
targets.missing_bridge: Specialize Mathlib's inverse function theorem to the normalized price chart.

targets.scope: Strict gross substitutes imply uniqueness of normalized equilibrium prices.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Continuity, homogeneity, Walras' law, positive normalized prices, exact strict-GS or irreducibility convention.
targets.missing_bridge: Formal maximum-relative-price contradiction.

targets.scope: Aggregate excess demand flexibility.
targets.weakest_assumptions: One precise theorem version, domain, dimension, boundary condition, and approximation/global convention must be chosen.
targets.missing_bridge: Source-level theorem selection precedes formalization.

targets.book_ref: Chapter 12, Walrasian allocations in the core
targets.scope: No finite coalition can finance strict improvements from its own aggregate endowment at supporting prices.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite consumers, individual budget equalities, strict support inequalities, coalition resource equality.
targets.missing_bridge: Map the book's selected blocking/core convention to the strict-part predicate.

targets.scope: Fixed-preference multi-observation equilibrium restrictions.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Exact original theorem and observable/latent quantifiers must be extracted.
targets.missing_bridge: Source theorem and quantifier-elimination interface.

targets.scope: Complete asset spanning yields allocation equivalence between sequential and contingent-commodity budgets.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite states/goods/assets, full row rank payoff matrix, no portfolio constraints, no arbitrage, positive numeraires.
targets.missing_bridge: Finite-dimensional spanning lemma and the two budget-set maps.

targets.scope: Termination, stability, and proposer optimality.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite two-sided market, strict preferences, one frozen acceptability/unmatched convention.
targets.missing_bridge: Executable DA state machine, invariant, termination measure, and rejection lemma.

targets.scope: Termination, Pareto efficiency, and unique core allocation in a strict housing market.
targets.weakest_assumptions: Finite agents/houses, bijective ownership, strict complete preferences, fixed blocking convention.
targets.missing_bridge: Cycle removal induction and core uniqueness.
